SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

Thornapple Grid Storage, Inc.
Series Seed Preferred Stock

THE SECURITIES OFFERED HEREBY HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED, OR UNDER ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS, AND ARE BEING OFFERED AND SOLD IN RELIANCE ON EXEMPTIONS FROM THE REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS OF THAT ACT AND THOSE LAWS. THE SECURITIES MAY NOT BE RESOLD OR TRANSFERRED EXCEPT AS PERMITTED UNDER THAT ACT AND THOSE LAWS PURSUANT TO REGISTRATION OR AN AVAILABLE EXEMPTION.

This Subscription Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of June 8, 2026 between Thornapple Grid Storage, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), and the undersigned subscriber (the "Subscriber").

1. SUBSCRIPTION

1.1 Purchase. Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Subscriber irrevocably subscribes for the number of shares of the Company's Series Seed Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the "Shares"), set forth on the signature page, at a purchase price of $2.4750 per share (the "Purchase Price").

1.2 Acceptance. This subscription is not binding on the Company until the Company accepts it by countersigning this Agreement. The Company may accept or reject any subscription in whole or in part in its sole discretion, and may terminate the offering at any time. If a subscription is rejected, the funds tendered are returned without interest or deduction.

1.3 Payment. The Subscriber shall pay the aggregate Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account the Company designates, on or before the closing date the Company specifies on at least three (3) business days' notice.

1.4 Closing. The closing occurs on the date the Company accepts this subscription and receives the aggregate Purchase Price. At the closing the Company issues the Shares in book-entry form and delivers a statement of holdings.

2. REPRESENTATIONS OF THE SUBSCRIBER

The Subscriber represents and warrants to the Company as of the date of this Agreement and as of the closing:

2.1 Accredited Investor. The Subscriber is an accredited investor as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, and has completed and delivered the accredited investor questionnaire attached as Exhibit A. The Subscriber shall promptly notify the Company if any statement in that questionnaire ceases to be accurate before the closing.

2.2 Investment Intent. The Subscriber is acquiring the Shares for its own account for investment and not with a view to, or for resale in connection with, any distribution within the meaning of the Securities Act. The Subscriber has no present agreement, undertaking, or arrangement to sell, transfer, or grant a participation in the Shares.

2.3 Suitability and Sophistication. The Subscriber has such knowledge and experience in financial and business matters that it is capable of evaluating the merits and risks of this investment, is able to bear the complete loss of its investment, and has no need for liquidity in this investment.

2.4 Access to Information. The Subscriber has been furnished the Company's certificate of incorporation, its capitalization table, its most recent financial statements, and the risk factors attached as Exhibit B; has had the opportunity to ask questions of and receive answers from the Company's management; and has received all information it considers necessary to make an informed investment decision. The Subscriber is relying on its own examination of the Company and the terms of the offering, and not on any representation of the Company other than those in Section 3.

2.5 No General Solicitation. The Subscriber is not purchasing the Shares as a result of any general solicitation or general advertising within the meaning of Rule 502(c) of Regulation D, including any advertisement, article, notice, or other communication published in any newspaper, magazine, or similar medium, or broadcast, or any seminar whose attendees were invited by general solicitation.

2.6 Restricted Securities. The Subscriber understands that the Shares are restricted securities under Rule 144, that they have not been registered under the Securities Act in reliance on the exemption provided by Section 4(a)(2) of that act and Rule 506(b) of Regulation D, that they may not be resold except pursuant to an effective registration statement or an available exemption, and that the Company is under no obligation to register them.

2.7 Legend. The Subscriber understands that the Shares will bear a restrictive legend substantially as follows: "THESE SECURITIES HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED, OR UNDER ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS, AND MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD, PLEDGED, OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED EXCEPT PURSUANT TO AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT OR AN AVAILABLE EXEMPTION FROM REGISTRATION."

2.8 Risk. The Subscriber understands that an investment in the Shares is speculative, that the Company has a limited operating history, that the Shares are illiquid and may never become liquid, that additional financings may substantially dilute the Subscriber, and that the Subscriber may lose its entire investment.

2.9 Bad Actor. The Subscriber is not subject to any of the "bad actor" disqualifying events described in Rule 506(d)(1)(i) through (viii) of Regulation D.

2.10 Authority. The Subscriber has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement, and this Agreement is a valid and binding obligation of the Subscriber, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency, and similar laws and to general principles of equity.

2.11 Residence. The Subscriber's principal residence or principal place of business is in the state or jurisdiction stated on the signature page, and the Subscriber has not been solicited in any other state.

3. REPRESENTATIONS OF THE COMPANY

The Company represents and warrants to the Subscriber:

3.1 Organization. The Company is a corporation duly incorporated, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with full corporate power to own its assets and conduct its business.

3.2 Authorization. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, and this Agreement is a valid and binding obligation of the Company, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency, and similar laws and to general principles of equity.

3.3 Valid Issuance. The Shares, when issued and paid for in accordance with this Agreement, will be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid, and nonassessable, and will be free of any lien or restriction on transfer other than those stated in this Agreement, the Company's certificate of incorporation, and applicable securities laws.

3.4 Compliance. Assuming the accuracy of the Subscriber's representations in Section 2, the offer and sale of the Shares are exempt from the registration requirements of the Securities Act and will be made in compliance with applicable state securities laws.

3.5 Capitalization. Immediately before the closing, the Company's capitalization is as set forth on Exhibit C, which is accurate in all material respects.

4. COVENANTS

4.1 Use of Proceeds. The Company shall use the proceeds of this offering for working capital and general corporate purposes, including the build-out of its Kalamazoo, Michigan pilot facility, and not to repay any indebtedness owed to an officer, director, or holder of more than five percent (5%) of its capital stock.

4.2 Form D. The Company shall file a Form D with the Securities and Exchange Commission within fifteen (15) days after the first sale of Shares, and shall make any state notice filing required.

4.3 Information Rights. For so long as the Subscriber holds at least 100,000 Shares, the Company shall deliver to the Subscriber unaudited annual financial statements within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year and an annual capitalization table.

4.4 Transfer Restrictions. The Subscriber shall not transfer any Shares except in compliance with the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws, and shall furnish the Company, on request, an opinion of counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Company that the transfer is exempt from registration. The Company may place a stop-transfer instruction with its transfer agent.

5. INDEMNIFICATION

The Subscriber shall indemnify and hold harmless the Company, its officers, directors, and agents from and against any loss, liability, or expense, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of any breach of the Subscriber's representations, warranties, or covenants in this Agreement. The Company shall indemnify and hold harmless the Subscriber from and against any loss, liability, or expense, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of any breach of the Company's representations, warranties, or covenants in this Agreement. The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice, the indemnifying party shall control the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, and no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party may be made without its consent.

6. GENERAL

6.1 Survival. The representations, warranties, and covenants in this Agreement survive the closing, together with Sections 5 and 6, including the governing-law and indemnity provisions.

6.2 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

6.3 Venue. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, and, where that court lacks jurisdiction, the state and federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware.

6.4 Assignment. The Subscriber may not assign this Agreement or any right under it without the Company's written consent. This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

6.5 Notices. Notices must be in writing and are effective on receipt, when sent to the Company at its principal office and to the Subscriber at the address on the signature page.

6.6 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, with its Exhibits, is the entire agreement between the parties as to its subject matter and supersedes all prior negotiations and understandings, written or oral. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties.

6.7 Severability. If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

6.8 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original, and delivered electronically.
